local_checks.invariant: Production VM deploy must be gated on passing CI checks, and repository content must not run with unrestricted root on the VM
local_checks.result: autodeploy.sh (timer every 2 min) checks out origin/main and runs deploy.sh with no reference to any CI status. deploy.sh runs repository-controlled node build scripts and npm ci as user baqueano, which per the service comment has passwordless sudo. deploy-production.yml 'checks' runs only on push to main (no pull_request trigger), so it cannot be a required PR status check and runs in parallel with the VM pull. The sudoers scope and branch protection are not in the repo, so this is needs_validation.

local_checks.invariant: Fork/untrusted PR code must not run with signing keys or write tokens
local_checks.result: Both workflows use the pull_request trigger (not pull_request_target). Fork PRs get no secrets and a read-only token. claude-review is additionally restricted to head.repo == repository. Same-repo PR authors already have write access, which lets them add a workflow that reads repo secrets, so exposing the keystore on same-repo PRs adds no new principal. Recorded as hardening. The claude-review prompt interpolates only repository and PR number, not PR title/body; allowed tools are limited to gh pr comment/diff/view and inline comments.

local_checks.invariant: Bot push to main must not carry third-party controlled content into an executable or HTML sink
local_checks.result: The workflow runs only on push to main / workflow_dispatch (main's own code), with contents: write. It commits website/data/territory-places.json containing Nominatim display_name labels. The consumer madriz-territory-map.js reads label into osmLabel and renders via textContent/el(); no innerHTML sink for label found. Not a finding. Its direct 'git push origin HEAD:main' implies that main accepts direct pushes from GITHUB_TOKEN (branch protection either absent or bypassed); this feeds the needs_validation blocker.

local_checks.invariant: Published APK should be the CI-built, signed artifact
local_checks.result: deploy.sh publishes the git-committed binary website/assets/BaqueanoNicaragua.apk as /downloads/baqueano-android.apk. There is no provenance binding, but the only actor who can replace it is a main pusher, the same principal as C1. Recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Values interpolated into .or() cannot add filter terms or change logic
local_checks.result: Holds. destination is constrained by cleanId to ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,120}$ (line 135) before interpolation at 329 and 393, so commas, parentheses, dots and quotes are impossible. The free-text q goes through textSearch (websearch), which is parameterized, not the .or() grammar.

local_checks.invariant: safeSearch output cannot break out of the ilike value in the .or() string
local_checks.result: Holds. safeSearch strips , ( ) % * \ (line 280), which removes the term separator and grouping, and the value is prefixed with % so it is never a quoted value. Remaining '.', ':' and '"' stay inside the ilike value. '_' acts as an ilike wildcard (only broader matching). The caller also needs the users.read permission (staff). Other ilike uses in baqueano-ops strip %/_ and use .ilike() parameters, not .or().

hardening_notes: baqueano-community react/report do not check that the target testimonial or comment is published, so reacting to a pending or hidden item by UUID returns its reactions_count. Gate on status='published', as the comment action does.

baqueano-community attach_media enforces photo/video count limits only in upload_url. Repeated attach_media calls with already-uploaded paths under the author's prefix can exceed photosPerTestimonial. Re-check the counts in attach_media.

baqueano-mirror accepts arbitrary document content without confirming that the Firestore write occurred. Consider re-reading the document server-side with the Admin SDK, or applying the firestore.rules field constraints (status, verified) to the mirrored data.

The staff role resolvers in community, reservas, sos and ops prefer the Firebase custom claim role/admin over staff_roles. Deactivating a staff_roles row does not revoke a still-present custom claim until the claim is cleared and the token refreshed. Confirm that the revocation flow also clears claims (owned by the RBAC unit).
baqueano-ops audit() records the client IP from the first X-Forwarded-For entry, which is client-influenced unless the Supabase edge overwrites it. This affects audit-log fidelity only.
reservas/sos resolveActor ignores the legacy claims.admin===true that community and ops accept. The role sources are inconsistent but fail closed.

A forged row therefore shows up in the victim's plan list. The attacker controls content through the unbounded travelStyle (index.ts:476, 573, 577) and the prompt. local_checks.result: Holds for identity and trust. logExchange always passes p_user_id=null and p_legacy_uid=null (index.ts:434-437). baqui_log_exchange is granted to service_role only (migration:193-196) and inserts rag_sources as trust_level 'unreviewed', verified=false (migration:176-181). local_checks.invariant: link_firebase binds the legacy Firebase uid to the caller's Supabase profile only with proof of both identities
local_checks.result: Holds: it requires a Supabase JWT validated via auth.getUser with email_confirmed_at, a jose-verified Firebase token (iss/aud app-baqueano) with email_verified, and equal emails (L569-579). identity_links PK (provider,legacy_uid) and unique(profile_id,provider) prevent relinking an already-linked uid; the upsert on conflict could overwrite profile_id only for the same verified email. hardening_notes: baqueano-identity set_role: the last-superadmin guard (L401-404) counts user_roles rows regardless of profiles.status, and set_status can suspend or block a superadmin without the same guard. baqueano-identity decide_verification and assertCanManageTarget rely on actor.profileId for self-action checks. Any Firebase-fallback actor (profileId null) bypasses them; bind the fallback actor to the email's Supabase profile id.

Hard-coded staff emails in firestore.rules (isAdmin/isSuperAdmin L31-51) and functions/lib/auth-middleware.js (L27-35), plus Firebase custom claims set by tools/set-role-claim.mjs, form further staff role sources that Supabase RBAC revocation cannot remove. local_checks.invariant: Anon-writable sprint_evidence_records stays ephemeral and isolated per X-Proof-Token
local_checks.result: RLS binds SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE to sha256(x-proof-token), so read and modify isolation holds. However, INSERT is unlimited for anon, the client chooses created_at and expires_at, and the repository has no job that deletes expired rows (no cron.schedule or delete anywhere). Expired rows therefore persist indefinitely. strategic_impact_report counts all rows, expired ones included, as the 'evidencias_sprint' education KPI (impact_alignment.sql 349). Candidate raised.

local_checks.invariant: Default-PUBLIC-execute RPCs get_nearby_* and match_knowledge_documents do not bypass RLS or disclose non-public rows
local_checks.result: All three are SECURITY INVOKER (no security definer), so table RLS applies. get_nearby_* filter on published or verified rows with LIMIT 50. match_knowledge_documents reads knowledge_documents, which already has a public SELECT policy. The knowledge_documents write policy FOR ALL USING(auth.role()='service_role') also serves as WITH CHECK, so anon cannot write. match_count is unbounded, but it returns only data that is already public. Not a finding.

local_checks.result: security_posture returns privilege and RLS booleans for a fixed list of relations, plus the server-only event names. hardening_notes: baqueano-identity set_role: the last-superadmin guard (L401-404) counts user_roles rows regardless of profiles.status, and set_status can suspend or block a superadmin without the same guard. A superadmin can therefore suspend or revoke peers until no active superadmin remains. This is an availability/lockout risk, not privilege gain.

baqueano-identity set_status: the result of auth.admin.updateUserById (L440) is ignored. If the ban fails, the profile is marked suspended but the Supabase session stays valid. RLS has_permission does check status, which limits the impact.

baqueano-identity decide_verification and assertCanManageTarget rely on actor.profileId for self-action checks. Any Firebase-fallback actor (profileId null) bypasses them; bind the fallback actor to the email's Supabase profile id.

Hard-coded staff emails in firestore.rules (isAdmin/isSuperAdmin L31-51) and functions/lib/auth-middleware.js (L27-35), plus Firebase custom claims set by tools/set-role-claim.mjs, form further staff role sources that Supabase RBAC revocation cannot remove. Revoking access requires a redeploy or a manual claim change.

The staff role matrices disagree: vigoronmixt@gmail.com is 'admin' in staff_roles (20261005000000 L46) but super_admin in official_super_admins (20260928192057 L47), so sync_staff_roles grants both admin and superadmin.
